suggestions.assertion: No em dashes (—) appear in the post body
suggestions.reason: The assertion scopes only to 'post body' but the SKILL.md policy bans em dashes from the title too. The output has an em dash in the Post Title ('AC Repair Cypress TX — Drain Line Clogs Before Summer') which the executor's grep checklist missed. Widening the assertion to 'post body and title' would catch this real violation. As written, the body-only check passes while a title violation goes undetected.

suggestions.assertion: A draft .md file is written to 04-gmb/posts/drafts/ (or copied to outputs/)
suggestions.reason: The 'or copied to outputs/' escape clause makes this assertion very easy to satisfy without the skill actually writing to the intended production location. In this run, the skill wrote to /tmp/ and the eval harness copied to outputs/. The assertion passed, but the draft never reached 04-gmb/posts/drafts/ — the location that post_pipeline.py would read from. A stronger assertion would require the file to exist at 04-gmb/posts/drafts/ in addition to (or instead of) outputs/.

No assertion checks that the post body contains a named Cypress community (Bridgeland, Towne Lake, Fairfield, etc.). The geo specificity is one of the most valuable aspects of a localized GBP post and the key differentiator from a generic template. This post does well on this dimension, but no eval catches it — meaning a post that mentioned only 'Cypress TX' and no neighborhood detail would also pass.

No assertion verifies that the selected CTA URL is actually live (returns HTTP 200). The executor checked this and documented it, but there is no eval assertion forcing that check. A skill that hallucinated a plausible-looking URL without verifying it would pass all assertions. Adding 'CTA URL resolves HTTP 200 when fetched' as a separate assertion would enforce this meaningfully.

eval_feedback.overall: All 8 assertions pass. The post is genuinely well-researched: real GSC data, live competitor checks, actual URL verification, 3-pass char-count compliance loop. The most meaningful gap uncovered is the em dash in the title that the executor's own checklist missed — an assertion covering the title (not just body) would have caught it. The CTA 'or most relevant' clause does real work here since no Cypress page exists, and that's a defensible pass.
